entities.summary: Gold hats are a very specific and rare type of archaeological artefact from Bronze Age Europe. So far, four such objects are known. The objects are made of thin sheet gold and were attached externally to long conical and brimmed headdresses which were probably made of some organic material and served to stabilise the external gold leaf. The following conical gold hats are known:Avanton Gold Cone, incomplete, found at Avanton near Poitiers in 1844, c. 1400 BC. Golden Hat of Schifferstadt, found in 1835 at Schifferstadt near Speyer, c. 1400–1300 BC.
